---
title: "SPEC-4.1.0-v001"
subtitle: "Gemini model update, tour overhaul, preview pills, search scope, always-maximized"
---

## Scope

Feature/fix release driven by user feedback on v4.0.5. Six areas: the Gemini
model 404, the interactive tour, launch behavior (popup vs. tab), the
preview panel and window cards, search, and version visibility.

## 1. Gemini model update (bug fix)

**Problem:** "Organize with AI" failed with
`404 — This model models/gemini-2.5-flash is no longer available to new
users`. Google has closed `gemini-2.5-flash` to new API keys ahead of its
October 2026 shutdown; new keys must use a 3.x-tier model.

**Fix (`services/geminiService.ts`):** both AI calls now go through a
fallback chain — `gemini-3.5-flash` → `gemini-flash-latest` →
`gemini-2.5-flash`. The first model that responds is used; a
model-unavailable error (404 / NOT_FOUND / "no longer available") advances
to the next candidate, so new keys get the current model while old
grandfathered keys keep working.

## 2. Interactive tour overhaul

Previous behavior: five steps, cards at hard-coded screen positions, arrows
only on some steps, no way to jump between steps.

New behavior (`components/OnboardingTour.tsx`):

- **Element-anchored steps with arrows.** Each step names a `data-tour`
  attribute on a real UI element. The tour spotlights that element (dim
  overlay with a bright cutout ring) and places its card on whichever side
  has room, with an arrow pointing at the element. Steps whose element
  isn't on screen fall back to a centered card.
- **Expanded coverage.** Eleven steps: welcome, windows sidebar,
  auto-name/undo, Organize with AI, search (including scope), detail/card
  views, working with tabs (checkboxes, context menus, keyboard),
  preview panel, export, theme, settings.
- **Stationary "Tour Steps" controller.** A persistent panel lists every
  step; clicking one jumps straight to it. It has an **End Tour** button,
  can be dragged by its header, and automatically moves to another corner
  if it would cover the spotlighted element or the step card.
- Step cards also gained a **Back** button.

## 3. Always maximized — popup removed

Previous behavior: the toolbar button opened an 800×600 popup which then
(optionally, via the "Open Maximized" setting) redirected itself to a full
tab; the Maximize button was kept left of the icon row so the popup
couldn't clip it.

New behavior: the extension **only** runs as a full browser tab.

- `manifest.json` no longer declares `default_popup`; clicking the toolbar
  icon fires `chrome.action.onClicked` in `background.js`, which focuses an
  existing dashboard tab in the current window or opens a new one.
- Removed: the Maximize header button, the "Open Maximized" setting (and
  its storage key), popup detection (`isExtensionPopup`),
  `focusOrOpenExtensionTab`, the 800px popup CSS, and the `hidden lg:`
  classes that hid Help/Export/Preview buttons at popup widths — the full
  icon row is now always visible.

## 4. Preview panel: window context and tab pills

The preview panel now has the **same layout in every mode** (tabs, windows,
AI groups), making it obvious what is being previewed:

- A header row with a **WINDOW badge**, the window's name, and its tab
  count.
- A **pill strip** with one pill per tab in that window. The previewed
  tab's pill is filled (indigo) and shows its full title; other pills
  truncate at ~130px and reveal their full title on hover. Clicking a pill
  previews that tab. Beyond 8 tabs the strip collapses behind a
  **"+N more"** toggle.
- Below that, the previewed tab's own row (favicon, title, switch-to-tab
  button) and the live content preview as before.

Window cards in card view now label their badge **"N tabs"** instead of a
bare number. The preview-toggle (eye) tooltip is now
**"Show/hide preview panel"**.

## 5. Search scope + bulk close

**What search matched before:** tab **titles and URLs only** — never page
content. That is now stated in the UI and controllable:

- A scope switch inside the search bar offers **"Titles & URLs"** (default,
  instant) and **"Titles, URLs & page text"**.
- Page-text scope lazily captures the visible text (`document.body.innerText`,
  capped at 500 kB per tab) of open tabs via the `scripting` permission,
  through the same 4-at-a-time concurrency gate as thumbnails, cached per
  tab+URL (500-entry LRU). A small counter in the search bar shows indexing
  progress. **Limits (shown in the scope menu):** sleeping (discarded) tabs
  are never woken for indexing, and restricted pages (`chrome://`, Web
  Store) cannot be read — both still match by title/URL.
- **Check All + bulk close:** a "Check All (N)" button checks every
  currently displayed tab (i.e. the current search results). With tabs
  checked, the toolbar shows **Move N**, **Close N** (with a confirmation
  dialog — closing is not undoable), and an uncheck button. Workflow:
  search "amazon" → Check All → Close.

## 6. Version number

- Bumped **4.0.5 → 4.1.0** in `package.json` and `manifest.json`.
- The version is now **visible in the UI**: the sidebar header shows
  `N Windows • M Tabs • vX.Y.Z`. It is injected at build time from
  `package.json` via a `__APP_VERSION__` define in `vite.config.ts`, so it
  can never drift from the released version.

## Verification

- `npm run build` (strict `tsc` + Vite) passes; `dist/` rebuilt.
- `quarto render` regenerates the book with this spec.

## Notes / accepted limitations

- Full-text search cannot see sleeping tabs without waking them (which
  would be slow and memory-hungry); title/URL matching still applies to
  them. This is by design.
- The Gemini model list will need occasional refreshes as Google retires
  models; the fallback chain makes that a one-line change.
